stem.text: Nitrogen monoxide reacts with hydrogen to produce nitrogen and water.
2NO + 2H<sub>2</sub> → N<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O
The rate equation for this reaction is shown.
rate = k[NO]2[H2]
Two experiments are carried out to investigate this reaction.
Complete Table 3.1.

explanation.text: In rate = k[A]m[B]n, the order with respect to each reactant is its power in the rate equation, and the overall order is the sum of the powers. Here the power of [NO] is 2 and the power of [H2] is 1 (no written power), so the overall order is 2 + 1 = 3. The orders come from the rate equation, not from the coefficients in the balanced equation.

reasoningChain: Read the power of [NO]: 2.
Read the power of [H₂]: 1.
Add them: overall order 3.

inferredMistakes.text: Taking the order for H₂ as 2 from the coefficient in 2NO + 2H₂ → N₂ + 2H₂O instead of from the rate equation.

stem.text: In experiment 1, the rate of the reaction is 2.80 × 10<sup>–10</sup> mol dm<sup>–3</sup> s<sup>–1</sup> when [NO] is 5.00 × 10<sup>–2</sup> mol dm<sup>–3</sup> and [H<sub>2</sub>] is 8.00 × 10<sup>–2</sup> mol dm<sup>–3</sup>.
Calculate the value of the rate constant, k, in experiment 1. State the units of k.

explanation.text: For the units, divide the units of rate by the units of the concentration terms: (mol dm<sup>–3</sup> s<sup>–1</sup>) / (mol dm<sup>–3</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = mol<sup>–2</sup> dm<sup>6</sup> s<sup>–1</sup>, which is the general result for a third-order rate constant.

reasoningChain: Rearrange: k = rate / ([NO]²[H₂]).
Calculate the denominator: (0.0500)² × 0.0800 = 2.00 × 10⁻⁴.
Units: (mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹) / (mol dm⁻³)³ = mol⁻² dm⁶ s⁻¹.

inferredMistakes.text: Giving second-order units (mol⁻¹ dm³ s⁻¹) because the units were not worked out from the overall order of 3.

stem.text: Experiment 2 is carried out under different conditions from experiment 1. The value of k for experiment 2 is 2.13 × 10–5.
In experiment 2, a large excess of NO is used. The initial value of [H<sub>2</sub>] is 1.20 × 10<sup>–3</sup> mol dm<sup>–3</sup>.
A graph of [H<sub>2</sub>] against time for experiment 2 shows that the reaction has a constant half-life.
Explain why the graph shows a constant half-life, referring to:

items: the overall order of the reaction under these conditions
the reason why this is the overall order under these conditions.

explanation.text: A constant half-life is the signature of a first-order reaction. NO is in large excess, so very little of it is used up and [NO] stays almost constant. The term k[NO]2 then behaves like a single constant, and the rate depends only on [H2]: rate = k′[H2]. The reaction is therefore (pseudo-)first order overall under these conditions. Both parts are needed for the mark: the overall order and the reason [NO] does not change.

reasoningChain: Constant half-life means the reaction is first order overall.
NO is in large excess, so [NO] is effectively constant.
So rate = k′[H₂] with k′ = k[NO]², a pseudo-first-order rate equation.

inferredMistakes.text: Saying only that the reaction is first order with respect to H₂, which the MS ignores because the question asks for the overall order.
Giving the order without explaining that [NO] stays (almost) constant because it is in excess.

stem.text: Calculate the half-life, in s, of the reaction in experiment 2 and state the time taken, in s, for the value of [H<sub>2</sub>] to fall to 7.50 × 10<sup>–5</sup> mol dm<sup>–3</sup>.

labels: time taken for [H<sub>2</sub>] to fall to 7.50 × 10<sup>–5</sup> mol dm<sup>–3</sup> = ........ s

explanation.text: For a first-order reaction, t½ = 0.693 / k (0.693 = ln 2). With the pseudo-first-order constant 2.13 × 10–5: t½ = 0.693 / 2.13 × 10–5 = 3.25 × 104 s.

Because the half-life is constant, count the halvings: 1.20 × 10<sup>–3</sup> → 6.00 × 10<sup>–4</sup> → 3.00 × 10<sup>–4</sup> → 1.50 × 10<sup>–4</sup> → 7.50 × 10<sup>–5</sup>. That is four half-lives, so the time is 4 × 3.25 × 10<sup>4</sup> = 1.30 × 10<sup>5</sup> s.

reasoningChain: Find the number of halvings: 1.20 × 10⁻³ / 7.50 × 10⁻⁵ = 16 = 2⁴, so four half-lives.
Time = 4 × t½ = 1.30 × 10⁵ s.

inferredMistakes.text: Using the third-order k from experiment 1 instead of the k given for experiment 2.
Counting the ratio 16 as 16 half-lives or 8 half-lives instead of four (2⁴ = 16).

stem.text: The overall reaction of nitrogen monoxide with hydrogen has a three-step mechanism.
2NO + 2H<sub>2</sub> → N<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O
Part of this mechanism is shown.

step 1 2NO → N2O2
step 2 ........ → ........
step 3 N2O + H2 → N2 + H2O
Complete the mechanism by writing an equation for step 2.

guidance: (M1 is for either correct LHS or RHS).

points.text: M1 one N2O2 and one H2 on L or one N2O and one H2O on R

explanation.text: Step 2 must link step 1 to step 3. Its reactant must include the intermediate made in step 1 (N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) and its product must include the species used in step 3 (N<sub>2</sub>O). The atoms that are left over are supplied by one H<sub>2</sub> and balanced by one H<sub>2</sub>O: N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub> → N<sub>2</sub>O + H<sub>2</sub>O. Adding steps 1, 2 and 3 and cancelling the intermediates gives the overall equation 2NO + 2H<sub>2</sub> → N<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O.

reasoningChain: Step 2 uses the intermediate from step 1: N₂O₂.
Step 2 makes the reactant needed in step 3: N₂O.
Balance with H₂ on the left and H₂O on the right: N₂O₂ + H₂ → N₂O + H₂O.
Check: the three steps add up to the overall equation.

inferredMistakes.text: Writing a step 2 whose products do not include N₂O, so step 3 has nothing to react with.
Not checking that the three steps add up to the overall equation, so H atoms do not balance.

stem.text: It can be deduced that step 1 is not the rate-determining step of the reaction.
Explain why.

guidance: I reference to NO without reference to order of reaction.
I N2O2 not in the rate equation.

points.text: no H<sub>2</sub> involved in step one (and H<sub>2</sub> in rate equation)
alternatives: only one species from rate equation
does not contain species in the same molar proportion as rate equation
if step 1 is RDS then order wrt [H<sub>2</sub>] = 0
step 1 does not include all species in rate equation
rate would be second order wrt NO only
reaction would be overall second order

explanation.text: The rate equation shows which species (and how many of each) take part in or before the rate-determining step. rate = k[NO]2[H2] means two NO and one H2 are involved up to and including the slow step. Step 1, 2NO → N2O2, involves only NO. If it were the slow step, the rate equation would be rate = k[NO]2, zero order in H2 and second order overall, which does not match.

reasoningChain: List what the rate equation needs: 2 NO + 1 H₂ by the end of the slow step.
Step 1 contains only 2 NO, with no H₂.
If step 1 were slow, the reaction would be zero order in H₂, so step 1 cannot be the RDS.

inferredMistakes.text: Saying only that step 1 'does not agree with the rate equation' without saying how, which the MS ignores.
Mentioning NO without referring to the order of reaction.

issues.note: QP 的 Table 3.1 没有表头行，左列是三个项目、右列空白供填写。站内表格 head 写成两个空字符串。
MS Guidance 原文 "I mol–2dm6s–" 后面还有一个很淡、看不清的字符（PDF 页面上近乎白色），照抄为 mol<sup>–2</sup>dm<sup>6</sup>s<sup>–</sup>，意思应是忽略漏写 s 的指数 1。
QP 给出实验 2 的 k = 2.13 × 10⁻⁵ 没有单位；从 MS 3(c)(ii) 的答案（t½ = 0.693/2.13×10⁻⁵ ≈ 32 540 s）看，这里的 k 实际上是准一级速率常数 k′ = k[NO]²，单位 s⁻¹。照原文抄写，AI 补充按准一级处理。
MS M2 接受 1.32 × 10⁵，相当于用 M1 的 33 000 × 4；照抄。
